Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed with Omar Sadar Saira Feroj, Advocates—For the Accused-Petitioners. 
Kazi M Ejarul Haque, Deputy Attorney-General—For the State-Opposite Party.

KM Nurul Islam and another ----- Accused-Petitioners

State, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in short, are that one Sarikul Islam alias Milton as informant on 10-9-2008 at 00.45 hours lodged an Ejahar with Motijheel Police Station alleging, inter alia, that the informant was agreed to purchase office space for 1145 sft from 10th floor of BH Belhasa Accom JV Limited, 103, Motijheel C/A, Dhaka at the rate of per sft Taka 4,000 and accordingly, total value was fixed at Taka 45,80,000. Thereafter, the informant as per contract paid Taka 5,00,000 on 8-3-2006 as advance through cheque No. 0215231 dated 7-3-2006 and thereafter, the informant on several occasions paid Taka 25,00,000 through cheques on various dates, as advance and, in support of payment, accused Sajjadul Alam, Marketing Manager of the Company, issued money receipts time to time in favour of the informant but the accused persons as per terms and conditions of sale did not hand over the said office space within June, 2007. On that, the informant asked to accused Sajjadul Alam to hand over the office space while he assured the informant that the possession of the office space will be handed over within June, 2008 and also requested to pay Taka 5,00,000. The informant in good faith paid the said amount of Taka 5,00,000 through Cheque No. 4489903 dated 29-2-2008 but in spite of that the accused did not hand over the office space within June, 2008 to the informant. At that, on 3-8-2008 the informant went to see his office space and enquired into the matter in presence of site engineer of the said project and found his office space is approximately 650/700 sqft while the informant informed about the matter to accused Sajjadul Alam and then the said marketing manager disclosed that the remaining office space will be handed over in favour of the informant at the rate of Taka 4,000 per sft although, the informant paid Taka 30,00,000 for the space of 1145 sqft. In this background on 5-8-2008 Project Director Mr KM Nurul Islam issued a letter and claimed more money of the informant and then the informant informed the same to the Marketing Manager when the said marketing manager told that after delivery of possession of the office space it will be decided. Thereafter, on 9-9-2008 the Managing Director of the company issued allotment cancellation letter and on getting the same informant informed it to accused Sajjadul Alam through mobile phone while the said accused claimed illegal subscription of Taka 20,00,000 and also told that if he is agreed to pay the same then accused Sajjadul Alam will take necessary steps to hand over the possession of the office space in favour of the informant. Upon the aforesaid allegation Motijheel Police Station Case No. 40 dated 10-9-2008 under sections 420/406/506/385/109 of the Penal Code was started. 

 5. Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused-petitioners after placing the first information report, submits that the allegations made in the first information report, even if are taken as true, do not constitute an offence punishable under sections 420/406/506/385/ 109 and, as such, the impugned proceeding is liable to be quashed to secure the ends of justice. He next submits that non-compliance of the terms and conditions of the agreement to purchase office approximately 1145 sft from 10th floor City Centre of BH Belhasa Accom JV Limited, 103, Motijheel C/A, Dhaka does not attract the ingredients of the provision of sections 406/ 420 Penal Code. Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed further submits that from a plain reading of the first information report it would manifest that the allegation of demanding subscription is vague, unspecific and preposterous in nature and thereby the allegation of demanding subscription as made in the first information report does not attract an offence under sections 385/506 of the Penal Code. Mr Ahmed further submits that admittedly there was an agreement in between the parties with regard to purchase office space approximately 1145 sqft from 10th floor City Centre of BH Belhasa Accom JV Limited, 103, Motijheel C/A, Dhaka and the informant at one stage stopped to pay the installment while the accused-petitioner No. 2 issued reminder letters on various dates to the informant but in spite of that the informant did not come forward to pay the installment as per agreement in which the authority of the company as per terms and conditions of the agreement cancelled the allotment letter and therefore, it cannot be said that the accused petitioners deliberately violated the terms and conditions of the agreement or the accused petitioners had any initial intention to deceive the informant. So, prima facie the ingredients of sections 420/406/506/ 385/109 of the Penal Code are totally absent in this case. Mr Ahmed further argues that the allegations as made in the FIR are squarely a civil claim and the informant as plaintiff over the self-same dispute has filed Title Suit No. 80 of 2009 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka for declaration that cancellation letter dated 9-9-2008 issued by the accused-petitioners is illegal and not binding upon him and, as such, the continuation of the instant criminal case is nothing but an abuse of the process of the Court which is liable to be quashed. 

 6. Mr Mahbubuddin Ahmed, finally relying on the decision reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38, submits that by now it has been well settled that if the FIR or petition of complaint taken as a whole and accepted on its face value does not constitute the alleged offence in such cases there can be no question of appreciation of the evidence or of investigation or enquiry about the truth or otherwise of the facts of the case where the High Court Division will be justified in interfering even at the initial stage before taking of cognizance to prevent an abuse of the process of the Court. 

 9. Heard the learned Advocates of both the sides and perused the FIR, supplementary affidavits, counter-affidavits and other relevant documents as filed thereto. It appears from the FIR that the project Director and Marketing Manager of BH Belhasha Accom JV Ltd, 103, Motijheel C/A, Dhaka took total Taka 30,00,000 from the informant on various dates but they did not hand over the possession of the office space of 1145 sqft situated at 10th floor of City Centre, 103 Motijheel C/A, Dhaka within June, 2008 as per agreement. It has been also alleged that the accused petitioners without handing over the possession of the said office space to the informant misappropriated the said amount of Taka 30,00,000 and accused-petitioner No. 2 also demanded Taka 20,00,000 as illegal subscription. 

 10. Upon a plain reading of the FIR it appears that the transaction in question was normal and routine transaction and, as such, the liability, if any, is civil in nature. As there is nothing in the FIR to show that the accused-petitioners had any initial intention to cheat the informant after receiving all installments against the office space in question. Rather, we find from the letter dated March, 2007 and 5-8-2008 as evidenced by "Annexure-I, J and K" to the supplementary affidavit dated 7-5-2009 that the accused-petitioners time to time issued letter to the informant asking to pay outstanding dues but in spite of that the accused-petitioners did not or could not make any response to that effect. So, it cannot be said that the accused-petitioners had initial intention to deceive the informant and thus, we are unable to see eye to eye to such submission of Mr Golam Arshad that the accused petitioners had the initial intention to cheat/deceive the informant. 

 (4) In a case where the allegations in the first information report or the petition of complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not constitute the offence alleged and in such cases no question of weighing and appreciating evidence arises. 

 (5) The allegations made against the accused person do not constitute an offence alleged but there is either no legal evidence adduced in support of the case or the evidence adduced clearly or manifestly fails to prove the charge.
